'''Fausto Calderazzo''' was an Italian [[Inorganic chemistry|inorganic chemist]]. He gained renown from numerous contributions in [[inorganic chemistry]] and [[organometallic chemistry]].<ref>P. M. Maitlis, D. B. Dell'Amico. "Fausto Calderazzo: Pioneer in Mechanistic Organometallic Chemistry". 'Organometallics, 2014, 33, 6989–7006. https://doi.org/10.1021/om5011963</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/S0010-8545(99)00081-8 |title=Celebration of inorganic lives |date=1999 |last1=Poli |first1=R. |journal=Coordination Chemistry Reviews |volume=188 |pages=1–22 }}</ref>  He was born in Parma, on March 8, 1930, where his father served in the [[Royal Italian Army|Royal Italian army]]. He died in [[Pisa]] on June 1, 2014, at the age of 84.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lunedì |first=Luca |date=3 June 2014 |title= È morto Fausto Calderazzo studioso di fama mondiale|trans-title=Fausto Calderazzo, world-renowned scholar, has died |url= https://www.iltirreno.it/pisa/cronaca/2014/06/03/news/e-morto-fausto-calderazzo-studioso-di-fama-mondiale-1.9354442 |language=it |work=[[Il Tirreno]] |location= |access-date=13 May 2024}}</ref>

==Life and education==
Fausto Calderazzoe entered the [[University of Florence]], in November 1947. He worked in the laboratory of [[Luigi Sacconi]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi= 10.1016/0010-8545(92)80044-R|title= Luigi Sacconi february 1911–september 1992|date= 1992|last1= Bertini|first1= Ivano|journal= Coordination Chemistry Reviews|volume= 120|pages= ix-xii}}</ref>  After the compulsory military service, Calderazzo joined the research group of [[Giulio Natta]], a future Nobel laureate in Milan. He was a postdoctoral fellow with [[F. A. Cotton]].  His first independent position was at the Cyanamid European Research Institute in Geneva (1963-1968).  There he was part of a team of future eminent scholars, including [[Carlo Floriani]].   For most of his career he was professor at the [[University of Pisa]].

==Research==
[[File:Crystallographic structure of (H(THF)2)(Nb2(μ-Cl)3(CO)8).png|thumb|Figure 4. Crystallographic structure of [H(THF)<sub>2</sub>][Nb<sub>2</sub>(μ-Cl)<sub>3</sub>(CO)<sub>8</sub>]|left|225x225px]]

===Metal carbonyl chemistry===
While in Milan, he discovered [[Vanadium hexacarbonyl|V(CO)<sub>6</sub>]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1021/ja01496a073 |title=Synthesis of Vanadium Hexacarbonyl |date=1960 |last1=Ercoli |first1=R. |last2=Calderazzo |first2=F. |last3=Alberola |first3=A. |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=82 |issue=11 |pages=2966–2967 }}</ref> He made seminal contributions to the mechanism of migratory insertion reactions, with emphasis on the stereochemical course of the carbonylation of CH<sub>3</sub>Mn(CO)<sub>5</sub>.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1002/anie.197702991 |title=Synthetic and Mechanistic Aspects of Inorganic Insertion Reactions. Insertion of Carbon Monoxide |date=1977 |last1=Calderazzo |first1=Fausto |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English |volume=16 |issue=5 |pages=299–311 }}</ref>  His team later (in Pisa) developed syntheses of Na[Nb(CO)<sub>6</sub>] and Na[Ta(CO<sub>6</sub>)].<ref>F. Calderazzo, G. Pampaloni. "Metal Carbonyl Complexes of Group VB Metals". J. Organomet. Chem., 1986, 303, 111-120. https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-328X(86)80116-4.</ref>

He contributed to the so-called "non classical" carbonyl compounds through studies on gold complexes.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1039/DT9910003017 |title=Halogenocarbonyl Complexes of Gold |date=1991 |last1=Dell'Amico |first1=Daniela Belli |last2=Calderazzo |first2=Fausto |last3=Robino |first3=Pierluigi |last4=Segre |first4=Annalaura |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Dalton Transactions |issue=11 |page=3017 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1039/C5SC02971F |title=How π Back-Donation Quantitatively Controls the CO Stretching Response in Classical and Non-Classical Metal Carbonyl Complexes |date=2016 |last1=Bistoni |first1=Giovanni |last2=Rampino |first2=Sergio |last3=Scafuri |first3=Nicola |last4=Ciancaleoni |first4=Gianluca |last5=Zuccaccia |first5=Daniele |last6=Belpassi |first6=Leonardo |last7=Tarantelli |first7=Francesco |journal=Chemical Science |volume=7 |issue=2 |pages=1174–1184 |pmid=29910872 |pmc=5975789 }}</ref>

===Metal halides===
[[File:Crystallographic structure of Au4Cl8.png|thumb|Structure of Au<sub>4</sub>Cl<sub>8</sub>|220x220px|left]]
Calderazzo extended his interest in carbonyl chemistry of the late transition metals halides.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1002/anie.199613311 |title=Molecular Structure of [Pd<sub>6</sub>Cl<sub>12</sub>] in Single Crystals Chemically Grown at Room Temperature |date=1996 |last1=Dell'Amico |first1=Daniela Belli |last2=Calderazzo |first2=Fausto |last3=Marchetti |first3=Fabio |last4=Ramello |first4=Stefano |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English |volume=35 |issue=12 |pages=1331–1333 }}</ref>  His group reported Au<sub>4</sub>Cl<sub>8</sub>, a simple mixed-valence gold chloride.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1039/C39770000031 |title=X-Ray Crystal and Molecular Structure of Au<sub>4</sub>Cl<sub>8</sub>, the Product of the Reduction of Au<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>6</sub> by Au(CO)Cl |date=1977 |last1=Dell'Amico |first1=Daniela Belli |last2=Calderazzo |first2=Fausto |last3=Marchetti |first3=Fabio |last4=Merlino |first4=Stefano |last5=Perego |first5=Giovanni |journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Chemical Communications |page=31 }}</ref>

===Early metal complexes===
Many of his contributions focused on early transition metals.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1002/anie.199411881 |title=[Zr<sub>3</sub>Cp<sub>2</sub>(O<sub>2</sub>CN ''i'' Pr<sub>2</sub>)<sub>6</sub>(μ-O)(μ-CCO)], the First Crystallographically Established Ketenylidene Complex; A Model for CO Reductive Cleavage on Metal Surfaces |date=1994 |last1=Calderazzo |first1=Fausto |last2=Englert |first2=Ulli |last3=Guarini |first3=Alessandro |last4=Marchetti |first4=Fabio |last5=Pampaloni |first5=Guido |last6=Segre |first6=Annalaura |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English |volume=33 |issue=11 |pages=1188–1189 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/0022-328X(95)00505-K |title=Aromatic hydrocarbons, carbocyclic ligands spanning several oxidation states in both Main Group and transition elements. Recent advances with Early Transition d Elements |date=1995 |last1=Calderazzo |first1=Fausto |last2=Pampaloni |first2=Guido |journal=Journal of Organometallic Chemistry |volume=500 |issue=1–2 |pages=47–60 }}</ref>  He carried out research on [[carbon dioxide complex]]es.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1021/cr940266m |title=Converting Carbon Dioxide into Carbamato Derivatives |date=2003 |last1=Dell'Amico |first1=Daniela Belli |last2=Calderazzo |first2=Fausto |last3=Labella |first3=Luca |last4=Marchetti |first4=Fabio |last5=Pampaloni |first5=Guido |journal=Chemical Reviews |volume=103 |issue=10 |pages=3857–3898 |pmid=14531715 }}</ref>

Starting with the preparation of V(η<sup>6</sup>-1,3,5-C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>3</sub>Me<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>, his group prepared many bis-mesitylene derivatives.<ref>G. Pampaloni. "Aromatic hydrocarbons as ligands. Recent advances in the synthesis, the reactivity, and the applications of bis(η<sup>6</sup>-arene) complexes". Coord. Chem. Rev., 2010, 254, 402-419. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ccr.2009.05.014.</ref>

==Awards and titles==
Calderazzo was a member of the editorial or advisor board of international scientific journals.  He was a member of the Société Royale de Chemie (1987), [[Italian Chemical Society|Società Chimica Italiana]] and [[Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]] (1989).  He received the A. Miolati award in Inorganic Chemistry in 1988 and the L. Sacconi Medal in 1998.
